newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: WTO ministers approve free trade declaration.
newsitem.headline: WTO ministers approve free trade declaration.

text.p: Ministers from 128 countries on Friday formally approved a declaration pledging their governments to work for wider freedom in world trade and to wrap up promptly a huge accord on information technology products.

Approval of the key document, shaped in weeks of North-South wrangling which ended in compromise at the World Trade Organisation's first Ministerial Conference late on Thursday, was announced by Singapore's Trade Minister Yeo Cheow Tong.
"The ministerial declaration is adopted," Yeo, the chairman of this week's conference, said to applause from fellow ministers.

The eight-page declaration forms a blueprint for the future work programme of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), including working groups to study links between trade, competition and cross-border investment.

Ministers also approved a plan of action aimed at boosting the trade prospects of the world's poorest countries and papered over deep divisions on the controversial issue of labour standards in the developing world.
"The ministerial conference has been an outstanding event in all respects," Yeo said.
